findings.issue: Plain `cargo clippy -p sc-treesitter` exits 0 but prints the config warning 'sc_agent_types::ResolvedApiKey::as_str does not refer to a reachable function'. sc-treesitter builds sc-agent-types with default-features=false, so the `secret` module is absent and the disallowed-methods path cannot resolve. The warning is also printed on the `--all-targets --all-features` run, where it does not fail the build. clippy.toml is byte-identical to origin/integrate/phase-a, so this sprint did not introduce it. It is a real consequence of the sprint's default-features=false dependency.
findings.recommendation: Add `allow-invalid = true` to that disallowed-methods entry. It is warranted: the entry is only valid when the feature is on, and the all-features workspace clippy still enforces it. Alternatively, accept the warning explicitly in the sprint doc.
findings.evidence: clippy exit 0 in both modes. The warning appears in the -p sc-treesitter lib and bin.

Coverage: workspace lines 91.48% against the 91.19 baseline. sc-treesitter is 90.68% per-crate against 87.74 (cli/mod.rs 100, extract.rs 95.4, git_io.rs 82.7, main.rs 85.3, grammar.rs 73.9, query.rs 70.6, render.rs 55.6). Branch and function coverage were not collected.

clap definitions (cli/mod.rs): `allow_hyphen_values` is set on --language, --query, --captures and --rev. Duplicate flags (--rev, --captures, --language) are rejected as INPUT_INVALID, tested in argv.rs. The `parse_rev` value parser calls `Rev::parse` unchanged, and `parse_captures` returns its own JevError. `value_parser_error` downcasts the clap error source back to JevError, so the messages reach stderr unwrapped. Help and version exit 0 on stdout. Every other parse error is INPUT_INVALID with exit 2, covering a missing PATH and 'a command is required'. All as intended.

Injection coverage (tests/argv.rs): `--rev=--output=<file>`, `--rev --output=<file>`, `--rev=-p` and `--rev -p` are all INPUT_INVALID, and a check confirms no file starting with 'pwned' is created. `--` allows a hyphen path.

git_io.rs hash-object: the environment policy matches sc_agent_types::git (LC_ALL=C, GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, the same five env_remove calls, --no-pager, -C). It differs only in setting stdin to a pipe, which is needed here. Input is bounded to 8 MiB + 1 before hashing. Writing stdin and then calling wait_with_output is safe: hash-object consumes all of stdin before it prints the 40- or 64-hex id, so stdout cannot fill first. stderr is null and stdin is dropped before the wait. A write error combined with a failed exit maps to extraction_failed. There is no wall-clock timeout on this call, which matches the shared git module's stated policy of leaving timeouts to the callers, so I am not raising it as a finding.

RepoRelativePath normalizer: the shared validation rejects '', '..', 'a/../b', backslash, drive prefixes, NUL, '.' and './', verified by the unit test. normalize() keeps only Component::Normal parts and rejects non-UTF-8 parts. Absolute paths are canonicalized (leniently, so a missing tail is kept) and must strip_prefix the canonical toplevel. In worktree reads the canonicalized full path is re-checked with starts_with(repo), so symlink escapes are caught. BlobSha is used for the sha through git::read_at_rev and a hash-object parse, which accepts 40 or 64 hex.

Panics: no unwrap, expect or panic in library paths. The only runtime expect is main.rs:46 `ScAgentErrorResponse` serialize, a documented-infallible fallback. The panic! calls are in cli/mod.rs #[cfg(test)] only.

ADR-SAG-0029 (c) in tests/cli.rs: the version and help tests moved to argv.rs, and cli.rs keeps the error-code assertions such as cli_missing_positional_is_input_invalid. The 'late --help is INPUT_INVALID' assertion was removed along with the argv-slot behavior. Under clap a late --help prints help with exit 0, and argv.rs covers `extract --help` as exit 0.

The `argv` and `cli` test targets are skipped under --no-default-features. This is by design (required-features=cli), so 'with and without --features cli' gives a skip, not a run, for the second case.
